subject: paediatrics
title: Primary Ciliary Dyskinesia, Kartagener and Laryngomalacia

steps.tx: Ultrastructural defects in motile ciliary axonemes impair mucociliary transport across respiratory and germline epithelium. The genetic disorder **primary ciliary dyskinesia** (PCD) is an autosomal recessive condition caused by mutations in axonemal structural genes like DNAH5 and DNAI1, which encode outer dynein arms. Absent or dyskinetic ciliary beating leads to chronic mucus stasis, recurrent sinopulmonary infections, chronic otitis media with effusion, and progressive bronchiectasis.
steps.say: Primary ciliary dyskinesia stems from dynein arm mutations in motile cilia. Lack of mucociliary clearance causes chronic sinusitis, recurrent wet cough, glue ear, and bronchiectasis.

vis.alt: Transmission electron microscopy of normal ciliary 9+2 axoneme versus outer dynein arm absence in PCD.
vis.caption: Ultrastructural ciliary cross-section showing 9+2 microtubule doublet arrangement and absent dynein arms in PCD. [Credit: StewardMD]

steps.tx: Random determination of embryonic visceral laterality produces complete organ transposition in half of affected individuals. The classic condition **Kartagener syndrome triad** represents a recognized subgroup of PCD comprising: situs inversus totalis, chronic sinusitis, and bronchiectasis. During early embryonic gastrulation, immotile monocilia in the embryonic node fail to generate the clockwise rotational flow required for normal left-right organ asymmetry, resulting in fifty percent probability of complete situs inversus.
steps.say: Kartagener syndrome presents with the triad of situs inversus, chronic sinusitis, and bronchiectasis. Immotile nodal cilia fail to establish left-right asymmetry, randomizing organ orientation.

vis.alt: Triad of Kartagener syndrome showing dextrocardia, situs inversus, sinusitis, and bronchiectasis.
vis.caption: Kartagener syndrome triad detailing situs inversus totalis, pansinusitis, and bilateral cylindrical bronchiectasis. [Credit: StewardMD]

steps.tx: Clinical hallmarks diverge between cystic fibrosis and primary ciliary dyskinesia despite shared bronchiectatic phenotypes. Children with PCD typically present with unexplained **neonatal respiratory distress at term**, developing daily year-round wet productive cough from early infancy, persistent rhinorrhoea, and recurrent glue ear. Unlike cystic fibrosis, children with PCD maintain completely normal pancreatic exocrine function, normal sweat chloride levels, and normal gastrointestinal nutrient absorption.
steps.say: PCD presents with term neonatal respiratory distress, daily year-round wet cough, and chronic glue ear. Unlike cystic fibrosis, pancreatic digestion and sweat tests are completely normal.

rows: PCD infants require oxygen at birth
Azoospermia in CF; immotile sperm in PCD

steps.tx: Non-invasive screening measures and ultrastructural electron microscopy establish definitive diagnostic confirmation. Screening for PCD utilizes **nasal nitric oxide measurement**, which reveals profoundly depressed concentrations (typically under 77 nanolitres per minute) compared to healthy peers. Definitive diagnosis requires transmission electron microscopy of ciliary biopsies obtained via nasal brushings, demonstrating absent outer dynein arms, inner dynein arms, or radial spokes, paired with targeted genetic sequencing.
steps.say: Nasal nitric oxide levels are profoundly low in primary ciliary dyskinesia. Electron microscopy of nasal brushings confirms missing dynein arms or radial spokes.

left.title: Nasal Nitric Oxide (nNO) Screening
points: Chemiluminescence analyser during tidal breathing
Values <77 nL/min have >95% sensitivity for PCD
Simple, rapid, non-invasive outpatient screening test

right.title: Transmission Electron Microscopy (TEM)
points: Biopsy of nasal or bronchial ciliated mucosa
Demonstrates absent outer dynein arms (DNAH5)
Gold standard structural verification of ciliary defect

steps.tx: Sudden aspiration of solid food particles represents an acute life-threatening pediatric emergency. The peak incidence of **foreign body airway aspiration** occurs in toddlers aged one to three years, whose lack of molars, immature swallowing coordination, and oral exploration predispose them to inhaling items like peanuts or seeds. The event classically begins with an initial choking paroxysm, followed by a variable symptom-free interval and subsequent unilateral wheezing.
steps.say: Foreign body aspiration peaks in toddlers chewing nuts or seeds. An initial choking episode is followed by unilateral wheezing and decreased breath sounds in the right main bronchus.

rows: Lodgement of object in laryngeal/tracheal inlet
Parents may witness or miss the crisis
Cough subsides, child appears deceptively well
Object settles into distal mainstem bronchus

steps.tx: Check-valve airway obstruction produces characteristic asymmetric radiographical signs. Chest radiographs reveal **unilateral air trapping hyperlucency**, where partial obstruction permits air entry during inspiration but collapses around the object during expiration, preventing air egress. Decubitus or expiratory radiographs demonstrate persistent hyperinflation and mediastinal shift away from the affected lung, while rigid bronchoscopy under general anaesthesia represents the definitive diagnostic and therapeutic gold standard.
steps.say: Expiratory chest X-rays show unilateral air-trapping with mediastinal shift away from the affected side. Rigid bronchoscopy is the gold standard for extraction.

left.title: Expiratory X-Ray Findings
points: Hyperlucent affected lung fails to deflate
Mediastinum shifts away from affected side
Depressed, flattened ipsilateral hemidiaphragm
Right main bronchus more frequently involved

right.title: Rigid vs Flexible Bronchoscopy
points: Rigid bronchoscopy is the absolute gold standard
Secures airway, allows optical grasping forceps
Flexible bronchoscopy used only if diagnosis unclear
Never use blind finger sweeps in oral cavity

steps.tx: Congenital supraglottic flaccidity causes the most frequent benign inspiratory noise in early infancy. The condition **congenital laryngomalacia** results from delayed neuromuscular maturation of supporting cartilages, allowing the epiglottis and arytenoid cartilages to prolapse inward during inspiration. The high-pitched inspiratory stridor begins in the first two to four weeks of life, worsens in the supine position, with feeding, or with viral congestion, and improves in the prone posture.
steps.say: Laryngomalacia is the most common cause of infant stridor. Supraglottic structures prolapse inward on inspiration, producing stridor that is louder supine and improves prone.

vis.alt: Endoscopic view of omega-shaped epiglottis and shortened aryepiglottic folds in laryngomalacia.
vis.caption: Endoscopic view of laryngomalacia showing inward collapse of an omega-shaped epiglottis and arytenoids during inspiration. [Credit: StewardMD]

steps.tx: Direct visualization during spontaneous respiration confirms characteristic dynamic supraglottic collapse. Diagnostic flexible laryngoscopy demonstrates an **omega-shaped epiglottis**, severely shortened aryepiglottic folds, and redundant mucosal folds over the arytenoid cartilages tumbling into the laryngeal inlet upon each inspiration. Over ninety percent of cases resolve spontaneously by eighteen months without intervention, while severe cases with failure to thrive, severe cyanosis, or pectus excavatum require supraglottoplasty.
steps.say: Laryngoscopy confirms an omega-shaped epiglottis and shortened aryepiglottic folds tumbling inward. Most resolve by eighteen months; severe cases with failure to thrive require supraglottoplasty.

left.title: Mild to Moderate Laryngomalacia
points: Stridor without feeding impairment or cyanosis
Normal weight gain and infant development
Reassurance and close developmental monitoring
Spontaneous resolution by 12 to 18 months

right.title: Severe Laryngomalacia Criteria
points: Failure to thrive due to feeding exhaustion
Severe chest retractions and pectus excavatum
Obstructive sleep apnoea and hypercapnia
Indication for endoscopic supraglottoplasty surgery
